title: The Streets: 7 Days
premise: Seven days on the block. Every decision is small. None of them stay small.
skeletonNote: PHASE 2 STRUCTURAL SKELETON. All prose is placeholder and marked [PLACEHOLDER]. No visual blocks: registries.json carries no Streets assets, and inventing cast/scene/prop references to make the skeleton look complete is out of scope.

design.deeIsNotAVillain: Dee never threatens and never punishes refusal. If he reads as menacing the player refuses on Day 3 and there is no scenario.
design.authoringRule: The player is not choosing between right and wrong. They are choosing what they are willing to spend, and what they have left on Day 7.

scoring.note: Scores are retained for schema compatibility and for the results log, and the values are real. playerVisible: false means they are never surfaced in player-facing scoring UI and never applied to the client's global stat pool. The Streets ends on trajectory and authored evidence, not on a number labelled INTEGRITY.

cast.name: Amara
cast.role: Has her own life and her own read

money.note: The only number the player sees. A plot fact, not a stat.

kaiStrain.note: Kai has no trust axis. He is friction, not a relationship being built.

s1d1_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Friday. Nothing is happening. The block, the flat, the last week of a term you have been half-attending.

s1d1_kitchen.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Mum is on a shift changeover and wants ten minutes. She asks about college in the way that means she already knows.

choices.label: Tell her where you actually are with it.
Give her the version that ends the conversation.

s1d1_kitchen_react.message: [PLACEHOLDER] She takes it, or takes what she's given. Either way she's out the door in four minutes.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] She doesn't push. That is not the same as believing you.
[PLACEHOLDER] She stops in the doorway and says something that isn't about college.

s1d1_street.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Outside, both of them want you. Jay has an evening planned. Tunde has a session at the cage and has asked twice already.

s1d1_evening_jay.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Chicken shop. Jay is funny for two hours and then, near the end, is briefly not.

s1d1_evening_tunde.message: [PLACEHOLDER] The cage. Tunde is training for something specific and does not make a thing of it.

s1d1_evening_alone.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Your room. The phone does most of the talking.

s1d1_close.message: [PLACEHOLDER] 23:40. A message from a number you don't have saved.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay's name is on the screen when it lights up.

s1d2_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Saturday. Jay is outside before you've eaten.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay is outside and has clearly decided not to mention last night.
[PLACEHOLDER] Jay is outside, four hours after you left him.

s1d2_ask.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He needs you to come somewhere and stand there. That's the whole ask. He is careful not to say more than that.

choices.label: Come, but you're not holding anything.
Not that. I'll do the other thing instead.

s1d2_help.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You stand where you're told for forty minutes. Nothing happens. That is not the same as nothing having happened.

s1d2_limited.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You come. You say the sentence once, in front of the person it was for. Jay looks at you a second longer than he needs to.

s1d2_decline.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He doesn't argue. He says fine in the voice that means the opposite and goes anyway.

s1d2_redirect.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You offer the version that costs you and not him. He takes it, surprised, and writes nothing down. You do.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Afterwards he is easier with you than he has been in weeks.
[PLACEHOLDER] Afterwards there is a gap in it that neither of you names.
[PLACEHOLDER] Afterwards you notice you are thinking about who saw you there.

s1d2_kai.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Kai is on the walkway with two others. Something gets said that is meant to be heard.

choices.label: Say the thing that ends it.

s1d2_close.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Home. Nothing has changed that anyone could point to.

s1d3_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Sunday. Word comes that you should come by.

s1d3_arrive.message: [PLACEHOLDER] A flat above the shops that is nicer than any flat you have been in. Dee knows your name and one thing about you that you did not tell him.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He knows your name and where you were standing on Saturday.
[PLACEHOLDER] He knows your name, which is more than you expected.

s1d3_dee.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He asks what you're doing with yourself. It is a real question and he waits for the answer.

choices.label: Give him the version that sounds like something.
Say very little and leave early.

s1d3_impress.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He likes it. You can feel exactly how much, and how easy it would be to keep doing.

s1d3_true.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He doesn't flinch. He says something about his own eighteenth year that you don't know how to hold.

s1d3_leave.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He walks you to the door and is nice about it, which is worse.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You get to the bottom of the stairs before you notice you are pleased.
[PLACEHOLDER] You get to the bottom of the stairs and feel like you failed a test you didn't sit.

s1d3_close.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Sunday ends the way Sundays do.

s1d4_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Monday. Three things want the same evening.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Monday. Amara has asked, which she does not usually do.
[PLACEHOLDER] Monday. Tunde has been counting on Thursday since Thursday.

s1d4_choose.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Amara. Tunde's session. Or the thing with Kai that is going to happen whether you are there or not.

choices.label: Amara.
choices.lockedLabel: Amara. — she hasn't asked you anywhere

s1d4_amara_1.message: [PLACEHOLDER] The bus stop, then somewhere neither of you picked. She asks a question about Dee that she should not know to ask.

s1d4_amara_2.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Later, walking back. She says the thing she came to say.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] She says it plainly, and waits.

s1d4_tunde_1.message: [PLACEHOLDER] The cage. Tunde has brought someone who runs the programme he keeps talking about.

choices.label: Stay at the edge of it.

s1d4_tunde_2.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Afterwards Tunde is careful not to ask whether you meant it.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Afterwards he tells the other man you'll be there Thursday, and looks at you while he does.

s1d4_kai_1.message: [PLACEHOLDER] The stairwell end of the walkway. Twelve people who all want to be able to say they were there.

choices.label: Get in the middle of it.

s1d4_kai_2.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It ends the way these end. Someone's phone has it.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It ends. Your phone has it. You have not decided anything yet.
[PLACEHOLDER] It ends, and Kai looks at you specifically on the way out.

s1d4_none_1.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Your room. Three conversations you are not in.

choices.label: Follow it on your phone anyway.

s1d4_none_2.message: [PLACEHOLDER] By eleven it has happened without you.

s1d4_after.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Tuesday morning. Two people ask you where you were.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Tuesday morning. Everyone already knows where you were.
[PLACEHOLDER] Tuesday morning. Nobody asks, which is its own answer.

s1d5_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Wednesday. Dee asks you to come by. It is phrased as an invitation.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Wednesday. Dee asks for you by name, through someone else.
[PLACEHOLDER] Wednesday. Dee texts directly, which he has not done before.

s1d5_stairwell.message: [PLACEHOLDER] The stairwell. He is exactly as warm as he was on Sunday. He asks how the week has been and listens to the answer.

s1d5_ask.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Then the ask. Small, specific, phrased as trust. He does not say what it is and you do not need him to.

choices.label: Not that — I'll do the other thing.
choices.lockedLabel: Not that — I'll do the other thing. — there's nothing left to offer him

s1d5_took.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It is in your bag and it weighs nothing at all.

s1d5_limited_n.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He agrees to the condition immediately, which tells you what the condition was worth.

s1d5_declined.message: [PLACEHOLDER] He is not angry. He is disappointed in a way that costs more than anger would.

s1d5_redirect_n.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You spend what you were owed. He takes it, and something in the room resets.

s1d5_react.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Outside. The walk home is the same walk.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Outside. You take a different route home and do not examine why.
[PLACEHOLDER] Outside. You are still carrying Tuesday's version of Monday.
[PLACEHOLDER] Outside. Nobody is following you. That was never the shape of it.
[PLACEHOLDER] Wednesday, late. There is more in your pocket than there was.

s1d6_open.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Thursday. It has landed, and not on you.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Thursday. Two people have already messaged you about it.
[PLACEHOLDER] Thursday. You hear about it fourth-hand, which is its own kind of information.

s1d6_news.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay is the one holding it. What he is holding is partly yours.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay is holding it. You still have the thing you wrote down in March.
[PLACEHOLDER] Jay is holding it, and part of what he is holding has your Saturday in it.
[PLACEHOLDER] Jay is holding it, and there is a video going round that you took.

s1d6_act.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You can put your name on it, keep it off, or let it sit where it landed.

choices.label: Keep it off you and off him.

s1d6_fronted.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You say it was you. It is true enough to survive being said out loud.

s1d6_covered.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You put a version together that holds. It holds.

s1d6_sat.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You do nothing, and doing nothing turns out to be a thing you did.

s1d6_tell_first.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Someone has to hear it from you first.

s1d6_close.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Thursday, late. It is not over.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Thursday, late. You are holding something that was not yours to hold.
[PLACEHOLDER] Thursday, late. Nobody has said your name. That is what you chose.
[PLACEHOLDER] Friday. There is a version of this week that is now a thing that happened to you.
[PLACEHOLDER] Friday. Tunde has stopped putting the sessions in the group chat.

s1d7_situation.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It needs something from you today that you either have or don't.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It needs something today, and there are two people who owe you a phone call.
[PLACEHOLDER] It needs something today, and you have already spent everything you had with everyone.

s1d7_move.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Four doors. Some of them are shut.

choices.label: Pay it and be done.
choices.lockedLabel: Pay it and be done. — you don't have it

choices.label: Call in what you're owed.
choices.lockedLabel: Call in what you're owed. — there's nobody left to call

choices.label: Go to Jay.
choices.lockedLabel: Go to Jay. — you two aren't there any more

s1d7_paid.message: [PLACEHOLDER] It costs what it costs and then it is closed.

s1d7_called.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Two calls. Both answered. You notice that you counted.

s1d7_jay.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay does not ask what it is for.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay does not ask what it is for, because you told him in March.

s1d7_alone.message: [PLACEHOLDER] You do it on your own, which works, and costs something you can't name yet.

s1d7_final.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Friday night. The block, the same as it was seven days ago, except for everything.

messageVariants.message: [PLACEHOLDER] Friday night. Four pounds and a week.
[PLACEHOLDER] Friday night. Nobody on the walkway has a reason to stop you.

terminal.consequence: [PLACEHOLDER] A week ends. It does not announce itself.
terminal.landing: [PLACEHOLDER] You work out on the walk back that the whole thing turned on about four minutes on Wednesday.

terminal.consequence: [PLACEHOLDER] A week ends the way most weeks end, which is quietly.
terminal.landing: [PLACEHOLDER] Mum is on the sofa with the TV on and does not ask where you have been.

choices.label: Say the thing to Kai.
choices.lockedLabel: Say the thing to Kai. — there is nothing between you to settle

terminal.consequence: [PLACEHOLDER] It does not fix it. It ends it, which is different and enough.
terminal.landing: [PLACEHOLDER] He nods once. Neither of you mentions it again.

reflections.title: PLACEHOLDER
reflections.text: [PLACEHOLDER] Wednesday was the hinge and you did not feel it as one.

reflections.title: PLACEHOLDER
reflections.text: [PLACEHOLDER] You said no on Wednesday and paid for it all week.

reflections.title: PLACEHOLDER
reflections.text: [PLACEHOLDER] You did the boring thing every day it was available.

jay.text: [PLACEHOLDER] Jay stops coming to the door.
[PLACEHOLDER] Jay knows exactly what you did and never says so.

mum.text: [PLACEHOLDER] She works it out in her own time.
[PLACEHOLDER] She notices that you picked up, every time, all week.

dee.text: [PLACEHOLDER] Dee is warm to you for the rest of the year, and never asks again.

amara.text: [PLACEHOLDER] Amara is still there in August.

finalMessage.text: [PLACEHOLDER] You paid for both and it cost more than either.
[PLACEHOLDER] It is not a story about a bag. It is a story about a Wednesday.
[PLACEHOLDER] You closed it yourself, and nobody will ever know.
[PLACEHOLDER] A quiet week is a real outcome.
